subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB704 (2026-09-06): the phrase that BUYS this rule was unusable above COBOL-85 until this landing - ORDER is the format's own optional word (measured: on the printed page only DUPLICATES is underlined) but the grammar spelled it as a `cobolWord`, and the 8.9 funnel, which screens IDENTIFIER occurrences position-blind, refused it as a user-defined word from 2002 (8.9 reserves ORDER since 2002). ORDER is now a lexer token with a cobol-words.json nameSlot row, so the phrase parses at every edition and `01 ORDER PIC X.` still draws COBOL0901 at 2002+ (conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb704-order-as-data-name). All three arms are evidenced: a) the USING-file order and, within a file, the access order; b) the input procedure's RELEASE order; c) the table elements' pre-sort relative order. Both formats realize it as an unconditional STABLE sort - CobolSort.Sort's store (SortWork, kb/Work PB3339) sorts each memory-sized chunk with a tie broken by release order (SortedOrder), merges only consecutive runs, always the last F (Cascade), and SortMergeCursor.Next gives an equal key to the EARLIEST run, so release order holds in memory and spilled alike (Format 1) and EmitTableSort emits a stable comparer (Format 2) - so GR4's undefined order is safely refined to the same one. Arm c) needs Format 2, which is 2002+; arms a) and b) hold at 85. Past the memory limit: SortWorkBoundTests.ASortManyTimesTheLimit_OrdersStably_WithinTheLimit_AndLeavesNoFile and SortWorkSpillConformanceTests (30,000 records, DUPLICATES IN ORDER).
